INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a polite way to disagree in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. You are wrong and silly
   B. I respectfully disagree
   C. Shut up
   D. Leave now

2. What are peers? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Animals
   C. People of your own age or class
   D. Only parents

3. Which interjection shows surprise? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck
   B. Ouch
   C. Wow
   D. Shh

4. What should you do in a reading competition? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Read very fast
   C. Whisper
   D. Read clearly with the right intonation

5. In a script dialogue, what comes straight after the speaker's name? (1 mark)
   A. A bracket
   B. A colon
   C. A full stop
   D. A number

6. Which is the first step in writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Draw the border
   B. Sign it
   C. Choose the theme and characters
   D. Write the ending only

7. Why should you ask permission before using someone's phone? (1 mark)
   A. It belongs to them and needs care
   B. It is a game
   C. Phones never break
   D. It is illegal to touch phones

8. What should you do if you dialled a wrong number? (1 mark)
   A. Stay silent
   B. Say sorry and end the call politely
   C. Call again angrily
   D. Shout at them

9. Which question should you ask about an advert? (1 mark)
   A. What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   B. Who cut it?
   C. What is the paper colour?
   D. How many pages does it have?

10. Which of these is an adjective in Fresh sweet oranges? (1 mark)
   A. oranges
   B. sweet
   C. sale
   D. for

11. What does interpret mean? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To explain what something means
   C. To tear it
   D. To sell it

12. Why should you ask an adult before giving your address on an online form? (1 mark)
   A. No reason
   B. To stay safe
   C. To make it longer
   D. To waste time

13. What is the purpose of the instructions on a form? (1 mark)
   A. To use up space
   B. To tell you how to fill it in
   C. To hide the title
   D. To make it hard

14. What does a class monitor do? (1 mark)
   A. Runs the school
   B. Drives
   C. Helps lead the class
   D. Cooks

15. Which is a rude phrase? (1 mark)
   A. Shut up
   B. Excuse me
   C. Please continue
   D. Pardon me

16. What is a stanza? (1 mark)
   A. A single word
   B. A rhyme only
   C. A group of lines in a poem
   D. The title

17. Why do we read poems? (1 mark)
   A. To enjoy language and learn lessons
   B. To hide feelings
   C. To stop reading
   D. To waste time

18. What is an instruction chart? (1 mark)
   A. A list of animals
   B. A drawing of a house
   C. A poster showing steps for a task
   D. A story chart

19. Why should each step contain only one action? (1 mark)
   A. To confuse readers
   B. To use fewer words
   C. To make it longer
   D. So it is clear and easy to follow

20. What does a red eight-sided road sign tell drivers? (1 mark)
   A. Go faster
   B. Stop
   C. Turn left
   D. Park

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

22. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

23. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)

24. Give three rules of good telephone manners. (3 marks)

25. Write two sentences using the interjections Hurray and Ouch. (2 marks)

26. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

27. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

28. Name two parts of an advert. (2 marks)

29. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

30. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — I respectfully disagree
   Polite words show respect.

2. C — People of your own age or class
   Peers are people like you in age or class.

3. C — Wow
   Wow is used for surprise.

4. D — Read clearly with the right intonation
   Clear reading with expression is judged.

5. B — A colon
   The name is followed by a colon.

6. C — Choose the theme and characters
   Planning comes first.

7. A — It belongs to them and needs care
   Respecting others' property is polite.

8. B — Say sorry and end the call politely
   Politeness matters.

9. A — What is being sold and how much does it cost?
   Buyers check product and price.

10. B — sweet
   Sweet describes the oranges.

11. B — To explain what something means
   To interpret is to explain meaning.

12. B — To stay safe
   Personal details should be protected.

13. B — To tell you how to fill it in
   Instructions guide the person filling it.

14. C — Helps lead the class
   A monitor helps the teacher lead.

15. A — Shut up
   Shut up is disrespectful.

16. C — A group of lines in a poem
   A stanza is a group of lines.

17. A — To enjoy language and learn lessons
   Poems entertain and teach.

18. C — A poster showing steps for a task
   It shows steps in order.

19. D — So it is clear and easy to follow
   One action per step is clear.

20. B — Stop
   That shape is the stop sign.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet, give your name, speak clearly, do not interrupt, do not call late without a reason, say goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hurray! We won the match. Ouch! I hurt my foot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Headline, picture, description, price, contact details (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
